note: Every rule that lives at the WRITER's boundary, in one document. This tier exists because no other tier reaches them: accept and format both RE-RENDER, and a re-render applies neither rounding nor shortening, so until this directory existed the whole of SPEC 4.5.4 was beyond the corpus and each implementation carried its own tests for it. BOTH ELEVATION TIES ARE LOAD-BEARING AND NEITHER IS DECORATIVE. Measured against the five wrong tie rules an implementation actually reaches for, each catches a different half and only the PAIR identifies round-half-to-even. 340.25 is 340.2 under the rule and 340.3 under half-away-from-zero and half-up-toward-positive-infinity, so it catches those two - and half-up is what the scaled trick Math.round(x*10)/10 does in both JavaScript and Java. 340.75 is 340.8 under the rule and 340.7 under half-toward-zero and half-down-toward-negative-infinity, so it catches the other two. Half-to-odd is caught by either. A fixture carrying only one of them looks like tie coverage and leaves two wrong rules passing. THE TIES COVER THE TIE RULE AND NOT THE OPERATION, WHICH IS WHY 0.15 IS HERE. Rounding a decimal place has two independent choices: which way a tie goes, and whether the value is rounded on its exact decimal expansion or scaled by a power of ten first and rounded as an integer. The two elevation ties above pin the first and are blind to the second: measured against a scale-first rounder that breaks ties to even, every other value in this document - both ties, both negative zeros, 512.449, 512.451 and the full-precision coordinate - gives the identical answer, so the whole tier could not tell the two operations apart. 0.15 does: its nearest double is 0.1499999999999999944, so its exact expansion rounds DOWN to 0.1, while 0.15 * 10 is exactly 1.5 in binary64 and rounds UP to 0.2 however the tie is then broken. Scaling is the larger defect of the two, because it disagrees on ordinary elevations rather than only on exact halves. A NEGATIVE COUNTERPART IS NOT NEEDED: -0.15 separates the same rounders that 0.15 does, and every scale-first rule that is correct on it is already caught by 340.75. NEGATIVE TIES ARE NOT NEEDED HERE and their absence is deliberate rather than an oversight: every one of those five rules is already caught by one of the two positive values, so -340.25 would add a value and no discrimination. Do not drop either number for looking redundant beside the other; they are not. A CLAIM THAT PART OF A FIXTURE IS DECORATIVE IS UNMEASURED UNTIL A TABLE EXISTS, because nobody writes that sentence after measuring - it is what gets written while explaining why a value was added. The table for these two values is above. The negative zeros are ones the WRITER CREATES rather than ones it was handed: -0.00000004 and -0.04 carry no negative zero into the writer and would carry one out of it in most languages, and format/ can only ever supply -0.0 as an input literal. `hidden: false` must not be written; the declared version 0.1.99 must be written back rather than the reader's own; the interior null at pip 3 must not be shortened away, because dropping it would move the time into the elevation channel.
